rulings.challenge_claim: The row's cited device "אֶל (oshb:Prov.3.5)" for 3:19's earth-founding clause is byte-false, and the row's own inclusio word for 3:18 is a blank span.
rulings.grounds: byte tier, re-spliced from verse_map_oshb.json independently of both packets. oshb:Prov.3.19 opens יְֽהוָ֗ה — the subject of both founding/establishing verbs — and אֶל does not occur anywhere in 3.19; אֶל exists only at oshb:Prov.3.5 as the preposition governing trust/leaning, a different verse outside the row's own 3.13-3.20 span. Separately, oshb:Prov.3.18 ends מְאֻשָּֽׁר, sharing the same triliteral root as אַשְׁרֵ֣י opening oshb:Prov.3.13 — the inclusio CLAIM itself re-derives true — but the row's rationale prints "which closes with  (oshb:Prov.3.18)" and observed_substrate_signals prints " (oshb:Prov.3.18) closing 3.18": both are literal blank spans where the Hebrew word belongs, confirmed by direct inspection of the row's own JSON bytes.
rulings.remedy: (1) Remove אֶל (oshb:Prov.3.5) as the device for 3.19-3.20's creation clause; the actual acting subject is יְֽהוָ֗ה (oshb:Prov.3.19) — cite that, or drop the claim. Test: collate.py byte-tier match between the cited ref's subject token and the claimed device. (2) Splice מְאֻשָּֽׁר into the rationale and observed_substrate_signals fields programmatically from verse_map_oshb.json (never hand-typed), then re-collate the row to byte tier — test: collate.py --ref oshb:Prov.3.18 must report tier=byte, not blank/none. WRITER-SYSTEMIC: אֶל (oshb:Prov.3.5) is reused as if it names "the LORD" across P02-003/004/006 in this cluster (and P02-001/002 in the sibling cluster per the sibling OL) — a recurring short-token-homography defect. The author-wave cure should be a p02-wide sweep of every אֶל/divine-name citation (pointed byte check per verse), not per-row spot fixes.

rulings.grounds: TWO components, one convergent with LF's item on this row, one distinct and additional. (a) DISTINCT, not raised by LF: oshb:Prov.3.21 reads בְּ֭נִי אַל יָלֻ֣זוּ מֵעֵינֶ֑יךָ נְצֹ֥ר תֻּ֝שִׁיָּ֗ה וּמְזִמָּֽה — it contains only מֵעֵינֶ֑יךָ ('your eyes'); no heart token (לב/לבב) appears anywhere in the row's own 3.21-3.26 span. The nearest heart tokens are לִבֶּֽךָ closing oshb:Prov.3.1 and לִבֶּֽךָ closing oshb:Prov.3.3 — both OUTSIDE and PRIOR to this row's span. The claimed eyes/heart pair is fabricated at the byte level: device_notes cites a device whose second half does not exist inside the row's own boundaries. (b) CONVERGES with P02-004/LF: the same אֶל-at-3.26 misattribution — oshb:Prov.3.26's subject is יְ֭הוָה, not אֶל. Same defect, not distinct from LF's item.
rulings.remedy: (1) Strike the 'eyes/heart' pairing from device_notes, or replace it with a defensible in-span pairing — the actual synonymous elements within 3.21-3.22 are 'eyes' (מֵעֵינֶ֑יךָ, 3.21) paired with 'life/grace' (3.22), not 'eyes/heart'. Test: a word-bound sweep for לב/לבב within the row's own 3.21-3.26 span must return zero hits before any heart-based pairing claim can stand. (2) Same remedy as P02-004/LF for the confidence-ground citation (part of the WRITER-SYSTEMIC אֶל pattern).

rulings.challenge_claim: The row's exclusivity claim that the father-quoting-his-father structure is 'unique across 62 verses in this part' cites the part's total verse count, not a digit-bearing sweep of the claimed narrative device.
rulings.grounds: Confirmed against the writer part plan: P02 = Prov.3.1-Prov.4.27 = 62 verses total (book strategy §9 tiling table), i.e. 62 is the PART'S SIZE, not a count of embedded-quotation/mise-en-abyme instances. No tool in SP/Prov/tools sweeps narrative-structure devices (confirmed against TOOLKIT.md's tool table — sweep.py covers token/skeleton/web string sweeps only), so the universal 'unique' claim has no adjacent digit-bearing sweep of the actual named object, violating the register rule (book strategy §8: 'Every universal claim... carries an adjacent DIGIT-BEARING sweep citation that NAMES the swept object and unit').
rulings.remedy: Either (a) strike the 'unique across 62 verses' universal claim and replace with a non-universal description (e.g. 'a mise-en-abyme structure not repeated elsewhere in this part's rows'), or (b) if retained, attach an adjacent digit-bearing sweep naming the swept object (a disclosed manual count of embedded paternal-speech-frame structures across the part, since no staged tool sweeps this). Test: check_universals.py must no longer flag this row.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row's claim that the repeated imperative is 'echoed again at the head of 4.7' misdescribes the verse's actual opening.
rulings.grounds: byte tier, re-spliced independently: oshb:Prov.4.7 opens רֵאשִׁ֣ית ('the beginning/chief thing'), not the imperative. The repeated pair from oshb:Prov.4.5 (קְנֵ֣ה חָ֭כְמָה, 'get wisdom, get understanding') recurs inside 4.7 but SPLIT, not head-positioned: קְנֵ֣ה חָכְמָ֑ה occupy 4.7's 3rd-4th word slots, and קְנֵ֣ה בִינָֽה occupy its final two word slots, separated by the intervening clause 'and with all your getting' (words 5-6). The row's 'echoed again at the head of 4.7' overstates both the position (medial, not initial) and the contiguity (split by an intervening clause, not adjacent) of the repetition.
rulings.remedy: Correct 'echoed again at the head of 4.7' to describe the actual split position: the get-wisdom/get-understanding pair recurs within 4.7 as its 3rd-4th and final two words, divided by the 'and with all your getting' clause — not as a head-of-verse echo. The underlying repetition-based cohesion argument for keeping 4.5-4.9 together remains sound; only the positional description needs correction. Test: a word-index positional check against consonantal_index.json/verse_map_oshb.json confirming the corrected position claim. NOTE: P02-008/OL raises a related, more granular version of this same positional-precision finding on this row; that item is deferred under the cluster's 8-item cap and should be reconciled with this remedy in the follow-on attempt rather than treated as a separate defect.
